extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent practitioners, patent stakeholders, and policymakers (Congress)
extracted.subtask_description: Advisory/report-level standards and recommendations for managing and improving USPTO patent operations, including patent quality, pendency, PTAB interactions, IT/AI modernization, outreach, and finance. Intended to guide policy, operational changes, and stakeholder engagement across the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a quality patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality patent is one that was thoroughly examined and prosecuted at the application for patent stage that can withstand post-issuance challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality patents afford patent holders reasonable reliance that they hold enforceable rights and inform the public of the metes and bounds of duly issued patents to avoid infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent examination quality (front-end)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the USPTO correctly rejects applications that fail to meet statutory requirements and issues patents for those applications that do meet statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO has compliance goals for work product; performance is measured by random sample reviews of examiner work to evaluate compliance with statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issuance proceeding quality (back-end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether issued patents are durable — i.e., able to withstand post-issuance invalidity and patentability challenges, particularly proceedings before the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations focus on whether statutory requirements are consistently applied in post-issuance proceedings and whether PTAB outcomes align with examination-stage actions; closing inconsistencies between Patents and PTAB is a priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency (timeliness) metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Pendency refers to the amount of time an application is pending before the USPTO, with both short-term average pendency goals and long-term absolute pendency goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via monthly pendency, application volume, and petition processing; pendency-reduction efforts are part of USPTO performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridging/closing the gap between Patents and PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce inconsistencies and improve continuity between the Patent Examining Corps (Patents) and the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) through shared processes and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a two-way learning loop: update IT to be compatible across units, enable cross-training, co-implement initiatives and pilot programs, and engage external stakeholders for feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize and improve data collection and sharing among USPTO business units to enable continuity, analytics, and decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes adopting compatible IT systems and data formats, implementing auto-classification and enterprise data solutions, and ensuring PTAB and Patents systems can exchange meaningful data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial intelligence (AI) modernization and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and deploy robust AI systems to support USPTO initiatives such as auto-classification, patent search, and data analytics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires sustainable funding and full staffing of AI technical and strategic experts; AI should improve external accessibility, inform policy on AI-related inventions, and support internal efficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity and IT resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen cybersecurity, resilience, and modern IT infrastructure (including cloud migration) to protect USPTO systems and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in defenses to thwart cyber-attacks, enable remote work continuity (as seen in pandemic transition), and pursue resilient architectures (e.g., cloud) and document standards like DOCX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant education and stakeholder training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide free educational programs to help applicants improve the quality of their applications and submissions (e.g., STEPP, virtual instructor-led training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage applicants, inventors, and practitioners to use trainings and provide constructive feedback; applicants play an important role in improving front-end quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity, and inclusion / access to patent system (Innovation Expansion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make USPTO services more accessible to individuals and groups that lack resources, know-how, or sophistication to navigate the patent system; increase diversity of inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Department of Commerce/USPTO initiatives (e.g., Council for Inclusive Innovation / CI2, Expanding Innovation Hub) and targeted outreach/programming to underrepresented innovators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper appointment and authority of the USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO should have a properly appointed Director with authority to make policy and administrative decisions; operating without a Senate‑confirmed Director is disruptive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim directors can manage operations short-term but may lack authority for critical decisions (e.g., review of PTAB decisions); PPAC urges timely appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arthrex — Director review remedy for PTAB APJs' appointment issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Supreme Court held APJs are inferior officers and remedied the constitutional issue by giving the Director discretion to review decisions rendered by APJs and issue final decisions on behalf of the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO must implement processes that allow Director review and final decision-making consistent with the Arthrex decision to cure appointment/oversight defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAS Institute rule on IPR institution
rubrics_metrics.description: When the USPTO institutes an inter partes review (IPR), it must decide the patentability of all claims the petitioner challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB institution decisions must consider all challenged claims, altering earlier partial-institution practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Fintiv factors in institution decisions (Sotera)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a parallel district court proceeding is pending, PTAB uses Fintiv factors to decide whether to deny institution of an IPR under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sotera is a precedential opinion addressing how to weigh these factors; PTAB and stakeholders should apply those factors consistently when parallel litigation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard in IPRs — BRI (Cuozzo)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court upheld the USPTO's regulation requiring the PTAB to apply the Broadest Reasonable Interpretation (BRI) standard in IPR proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BRI affects how claims are interpreted in AIA proceedings and impacts institution/outcome strategy for parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government entity standing in AIA proceedings (Return Mail)
rubrics_metrics.description: A government agency cannot challenge patents using IPR, PGR, and CBM because the AIA's use of 'person' is presumed to exclude the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government agencies are generally precluded from filing post-grant challenges under AIA mechanisms; impacts who can be petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO authority on AIA petition timeliness (Thryv)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court held the USPTO has unreviewable authority to decide whether a party properly petitioned under the AIA within one year of being served a complaint for patent infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB determinations on statutory timeliness under the one-year bar are generally not reviewable by courts; petitioners should ensure compliance and consider administrative remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement limits on functional claiming (Amgen)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional claims to antibodies based on what they bind to can be invalid under 35 U.S.C. § 112 for lack of enablement if undue experimentation is required to make and use the full scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional/means/way claiming can be vulnerable to enablement attacks; applicants should provide sufficient disclosure to avoid undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent eligibility scrutiny for abstract ideas (Yu v. Apple)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may find patents invalid under 35 U.S.C. § 101 when claims are directed to abstract ideas (e.g., enhancing photographs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanical and software-adjacent claims may be susceptible to eligibility challenges; patentees and examiners should evaluate claims under current §101 jurisprudence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of assignor estoppel (Minerva)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignor estoppel prohibits inventors from challenging their patents after assignment, but its scope is limited to situations where the assignor's invalidity claim contradicts explicit or implicit representations made in the assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignor estoppel does not apply in certain situations (e.g., claims to future inventions, legal developments rendering representations irrelevant, or claim changes post-assignment); parties should analyze estoppel carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB quality improvement initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB should pursue quality improvement programs such as 'Enabling Continuous Learning', targeted rulemaking, and operational programs to raise the quality of PTAB decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives include external/internal training, hearings operations improvements, IT upgrades, and outreach; these aim to increase consistency and decision durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal and external review mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use internal review processes and external quality surveys (EQS) to evaluate examiner and PTAB compliance with statutory and procedural standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual and random samples inform compliance goals; both internal audits and external stakeholder feedback are important for continuous quality measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions processing and impact on pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions (e.g., to revive, to accept late papers, for extension, for rehearing) affect workload and pendency and must be tracked and managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring petition volumes and processing times is part of pendency management; policy should address commonly-filed petition types to reduce backlogs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte appeals monitoring and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Track ex parte appeal statistics, conduct outreach, and pursue ongoing activities to improve appeal handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and report ex parte appeal metrics; engage stakeholders to understand appeal-related quality/performance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT systems and PTAB/Patents interoperability
rubrics_metrics.description: Upgrade IT systems (PTAB website, P-TACTS/PTAB Center, Patent Examination Data System) to ensure compatibility, data exchange, and improved stakeholder access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IT improvements should support hearing operations, public access to case data, cross-unit analytics, and modernization goals like cloud migration and DOCX support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee reserves and financial metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain optimal reserve levels (defined for Patents as three months of operating requirements) and pursue access to previously collected fees held at Treasury subject to Congressional approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate reserves mitigate economic uncertainty and enable infrastructure and service improvements; PPAC recommends Congress release previously collected user fees to reach optimal levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee adjustments and budget transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust user fees and maintain transparent budget reporting and historical trend analysis to support USPTO operations and modernization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee-setting should consider operational needs (IT, AI, staffing) and stakeholder impacts; monitor previously collected fees not available and report impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional outreach offices and stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate and evaluate Regional Offices to increase stakeholder access and perform outreach domestically and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional offices should provide training, stakeholder engagement, and localized services; evaluate performance and resource needs to maximize outreach effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: International cooperation, work-sharing, and IP forum engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in international fora (IP5, ID5, WIPO) and pursue work-sharing and harmonization efforts to improve patent examination quality and efficiency globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work-sharing can reduce duplication, enhance search resources, and align practices across major offices; monitor IP and trade implications and maintain active international engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative priorities and pilot programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and advise on pending legislation and pilots affecting the patent system (e.g., sequenced examination pilot, patent small claims tribunal, patent bar eligibility changes, subject matter eligibility study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC should communicate recommendations to Congress and track legislative impacts on quality, access, and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing AI policies at the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft clear USPTO policies for AI-related inventions and for the use of AI within the Office (governing auto-classification, AI-assisted search, and decision-support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy development should balance stakeholder input, legal frameworks, and operational deployment; provide guidance for inventors and examiners on AI-disclosed innovations and AI-assisted tools.
